items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: John Hicks and Billy Hart — all these great musicians that I admire

ctx.x: Is it a challenge — you’re both practicing musicians and artists. I think I know the answer to this but is it a challenging way to make a living?

Sure is. Really is. Especially right now. You know because the — how do we say it — not the template, but what has worked for so long does not work as well anymore. So what we’ve been conditioned in the last — rehearse a band, go out on tour, come home, make a record, everybody you know goes and does their own thing for a bit, then come back together. Yeah, it’s — with the clubs, you know so many of the clubs, arts presenters, funding cut back for the art presenters received. It’s in a changing environment for…

Pullen and John Hicks and Billy Hart — all these great musicians that I admire, they’ve all just lived off their musical performance. Their playing. Their artistic endeavors. Their creative drive and their expertise in being hired. That’s gone. So I don’t know. It’s just different to really have to, in my case I’m trying to maybe open up a bit more to collaborating with more musicians and so that will allow me to stay in a creative space which is what I really thrive on. I love collaborating, I love throwing…
